checks_run.procedure: Line-by-line source review of every product change in 8488e7a..aa0a68f and the full files it touches: access/request.ts, access/denials.ts, transformations/register-kit.ts openWrite, evidence/routes.ts (three-phase upload, start-up sweep hook), evidence/store.ts (sweep, receive cleanup), identity/routes.ts (principalFor, login), identity/oidc.ts, platform/in-flight.ts, server.ts, main.ts and packages/db/src/pool.ts. The review checks for weakened authorization, CSRF, optimistic concurrency, the audit trail, the evidence size limit and raw sha256, BE16/BE17 connection and pool behaviour, and OIDC state/nonce/PKCE/binding, and scans the added lines for risky constructs.
checks_run.command: git diff 8488e7a..aa0a68f -- apps packages; git diff --stat 8488e7a..aa0a68f -- . ':!docs/delivery'; grep scan of added lines (diff-scan.log)
checks_run.expected: No regression in authorization, CSRF, If-Match/version checks, audit, size limit or sha256, pool/connection behaviour or the OIDC login/callback; no new dependency, secret, CDN or remote call
checks_run.actual:
No regression found.
- Authorization and CSRF: the preValidation hook still resolves the session and loads the grants via the same resolution, now factored into principalFor. CSRF and origin checks are unchanged. refreshPrincipal only re-resolves the SAME token and requires the SAME user id, and it fails closed (no resolver or null result gives 401). Re-authorisation can only narrow authority, never widen it.
- Optimistic concurrency, audit and denials: the If-Match check on the FOR UPDATE row, the version-guarded update and the evidence.upload_content audit are unchanged. commitTimeDenial keeps the denial, so the failed-mutation audit still fires.
- Upload limits: store.receive keeps the 25 MiB limit and the streaming sha256 over the raw bytes. Its cleanup now removes the temporary even when handle.close() fails.
- OIDC: prepareLogin and saveLoginState keep state, nonce and PKCE server-side and store sha256(state) and sha256(binding). The cookie is set after the insert. The callback code is unchanged.
- Shutdown tracking: in-flight.ts wraps every handler registered after it, which is all routes (server.ts order). It returns the handler's own promise, and settled() is bounded. main.ts orders app.close -> settled(3 s) -> db.destroy -> exit inside the 10 s backstop.
- Start-up sweep: readdir withFileTypes never follows symlinked directories below the root. The name filter is strict (/^uuid\.part$/), the depth is exactly 3, lstat confirms a regular file, the cutoff is 1 h by mtime, it runs in the background, it is tracked, and failures are logged at warn.
- Diff scan: package.json and the lockfile are unchanged, there is no new dependency, and no product line adds fetch, eval, exec, a URL or a secret. The matches are all in test files: a loopback IdP, child_process in the shutdown test, and a synthetic marker asserted NOT to be logged.

checks_run.procedure: Adversarial round-13 probe, group S (stale authority at phase boundaries). S1: role DOWNGRADE WL -> AUD mid-body. S2: the item's owner reassigned away from the uploader mid-body. S3: MEASUREMENT of the residual, where phase 3 waits on the item's row lock (FOR KEY SHARE held by another transaction) while a revocation commits. (Archive mid-body = r12 Q2; re-grant race = candidate commit-time-auth.test.ts; idle/absolute expiry and disabled user = candidate tests, all passing.)
checks_run.command: probe-runs.sh: with-pg.sh 29985|29986 pnpm vitest run --project integration apps/api/test/integration/zz-sec-r13-probe.test.ts
checks_run.environment: probe clone $TMPDIR/r13p at 5699f72; Node 22.22.2 (LANG unset) and 24.21.0 (LANG=C.UTF-8)
checks_run.expected: S1 403 + authorization.denied audit, nothing stored; S2 never 200, nothing stored; S3 consistent (either refused with nothing stored, or committed with its object)
checks_run.actual:
Same result on both Node versions:
- S1: 403 forbidden, one authorization.denied audit '... requires evidence.create', no row, version unchanged, no object; the downgraded user still reads the item (200).
- S2: 403 forbidden, nothing stored.
- S3: 200, with one row and its object (consistent). This confirms that a revocation committing during phase 3's lock wait does not stop the commit. That is the documented residual (phase 3's own transaction): only a concurrent transaction holding the item's row lock can lengthen it, none waits on a client since BE17, and statement_timeout bounds it at 30 s. The uploader cannot extend it through the API. It is recorded as an observation, not a finding.

checks_run.procedure:
Adversarial round-13 probe, group V (start-up sweep).
- V1 traversal, symlinks and names: one real stale <uuid>.part at depth 3, plus decoys.
  - Kept by design: a fresh .part, a stale final object, .part at depth 2 and 4, an upper-case UUID, <uuid>.part.bak, a DIRECTORY named <uuid>.part.
  - Outside the store: a stale <uuid>.part SYMLINK to an outside file, and a depth-0 directory SYMLINK to an outside tree that holds a stale .part.
- V2: a live upload on instance A while instance B starts on the same store.
- V3: the live .part back-dated by 2 h, beyond the documented clock-skew margin, then B's sweep.
checks_run.environment: as SEC-R13-19; per-test evidence store directories under $TMPDIR
checks_run.expected: V1 only the real stale .part removed, everything else (incl. outside targets) intact; V2 removed 0 and the upload commits 200; V3 fail closed: no committed row pointing at a missing object
checks_run.actual:
Same on both Node versions:
- V1: removed 1 / keptFresh 1. Every decoy survives, including the symlinked outside file and the outside tree. One info log line with the relative key o1/t1/e1/<uuid>.part.
- V2: B's sweep removed 0, keptFresh 1; A's upload then 200 with one row.
- V3: B's sweep removed the live .part. A's finalise rename then fails (ENOENT), answered 500 internal with the error-level 'unhandled error' log; the probe induced this fault deliberately and asserts it. No content row, current_content_id null, no object. This needs >1 h of clock skew between hosts or a >1 h body, which requestTimeout (300 s) precludes. Integrity holds either way.

checks_run.procedure: Adversarial round-13 probe, X1. Start the REAL API process (src/main.ts). The probe holds a FOR UPDATE row lock on an evidence item, sends a JSON PATCH to that item (its handler blocks inside the transaction), then sends SIGTERM. Measure the exit time and code, then verify that the PATCH did not commit.
checks_run.environment: as SEC-R13-19; child process node --conditions=@mth/source apps/api/src/main.ts on a random port 26000-31999
checks_run.expected: exit within grace (5 s) + settle (3 s) + backstop bound (10 s total, < 11.5 s asserted); PATCH not committed
checks_run.actual: On both Node versions the process exits at 10.0 s (10017 ms) with code 1, by the backstop. Log sequence: 'shutting down' -> warn 'shutdown grace period elapsed' -> warn 'request handlers still running after the settle period; closing the database anyway' (pending 1) -> error (level 50) 'shutdown did not finish in time; exiting'. The probe induced this level-50 line deliberately and asserts it; it is the backstop working as designed. The item keeps version 1 and its original title. The settle wait cannot hold the process past the backstop.

summary:
DG2 round 13, candidate 6824b8b8 (source aa0a68f, 556 files; recomputed in the working tree and in a clean clone). F-DG2-440 and F-DG2-441 are CLOSED_VERIFIED.
- F-DG2-440: my round-12 Q1 (grant revoked mid-body) now gets 403, and Q1b (logout mid-body) gets 401; nothing is stored in either case (round 12: 200 for both). New adversarial checks pass:
  - a role downgrade mid-body gives 403 with an authorization.denied audit;
  - an owner reassignment mid-body gives 403.
  The remaining window is the documented one (phase 3's own transaction). I measured it, including a row-lock wait, and record it as an observation.
- F-DG2-441: my round-12 Q7 now shows no session idle in transaction while the IdP hangs, and /me answers in 18-22 ms (round 12: 9 s). My own AST sweep finds no other non-database await inside a transaction besides the documented finalise.
- BE18A shutdown and sweep add no new hole:
  - the sweep ignores symlinks, wrong depths, wrong names and directories;
  - it keeps a live temporary on shared storage;
  - when clock skew exceeds the margin, it fails closed with no committed row;
  - a handler stuck on the database cannot hold shutdown past the 10 s backstop.
- All required checks ran and passed: typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint (161 ops), no-CDN, format, unit 796/796 on Node 22 and 24 and under load, integration 612/612 in both locale runs (migrations 0001-0019, AUD sweep 146/146), and historical DG0 and DG1 validation.
- Every error-level line in the cited logs comes from a deliberately induced fault, and each is explained.
- No new findings.
